options.title: Pygame pattern puzzle
options.pitch: Create a sequence-recall puzzle for a school activity club. Keep graphics simple and assess the Python logic.
requirements: Store a target pattern and player attempts in one-dimensional lists. Use separate functions for round setup, input validation, scoring and summary.
Support a repeatable practice mode with a fixed pattern, increasing challenge and a clear restart/quit route.
Save a synthetic session summary to a text file. Keep event handling and display separate from assessable logic.
resources: Python 3; optional school-approved Pygame installation; keyboard and screen.
Use coloured rectangles or original text, so no downloaded assets are necessary.
Included puzzle-logic.py contains unfinished function contracts; fixture data and expected cases accompany it.
tests: Pattern [1,3,2], attempt [1,3,2]: 3 matching positions.
Pattern [1,3,2], attempt [1,2,3]: 1 matching position.
Reject symbols outside the permitted range; quit and restart leave a consistent state.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.title: Python experiments: queue simulator
options.pitch: Model a fictional service desk and compare two staffing configurations. Assess software quality rather than scientific sophistication.
requirements: Represent queue lengths over discrete ticks in a one-dimensional list. Supply arrivals and service capacity as validated inputs.
Write functions for one simulation step, a complete run and a summary. Queue length cannot fall below zero.
Use deterministic input sequences for tests, then compare configurations and state the model’s assumptions. Save results as text.
resources: Python 3 with standard library only; no headset or internet required.
Included arrivals.csv, queue-logic.py stubs and manual expected cases.
Optional Pygame graph comes after the tested console model.
tests: Step rule: next queue = max(0, queue + arrivals - capacity).
Start 0, arrivals [2,0,3], capacity 1: queue trace [1,0,2].
No arrivals yields zero queue; negative arrivals/capacity must be rejected.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.title: Python experiments: a simple habitat model
options.pitch: Develop a clearly labelled fictional population model for a science display.
requirements: Store population at each step in a one-dimensional list. Use validated initial population, births and losses.
Separate update logic from display. Prevent negative population and define rounding explicitly.
Compare fixed parameter sets using repeatable runs, record assumptions and save a summary.
resources: Python standard library and synthetic starting values.
Teacher supplies a simple update rule before issue; no biology knowledge marks.
Common requirements, schedule and testing templates included.
tests: For rule max(0,population+births-losses), 10+2-3 gives 9.
Zero population and losses larger than population follow the declared rule.
Repeat identical inputs and check identical output.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.title: Club order manager
options.pitch: Adapt the textbook’s familiar order context into a fresh client brief with individually assigned values.
requirements: Validate invented order IDs and non-negative whole quantities. Use functions and a list for current-session orders.
Calculate integer-cent costs, append records and preserve existing runs. A save failure must not claim success.
Show totals, the first largest-order position and an empty-session message. Use a new price and scenario for an issued assessment.
resources: Python standard library; existing project workbook and unfinished starter are public practice references.
Teacher must replace familiar worked values and require independent transfer.
Use the common evidence templates and a writable disposable folder.
tests: Write expectations using the issued price, including a zero order.
Empty session and tied largest values follow the brief.
Two program runs retain both saved records.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.title: Interactive trail challenge
options.pitch: Build a text-based resource-management adventure for a fictional walking trail.
requirements: Store route choices or resources in one-dimensional lists and implement branches and loops using functions.
Validate menu choices and update a resource total under explicitly defined rules.
Save a session summary and explain at least two alternative design choices.
resources: Python standard library; teacher-written short scenario and simple rule sheet.
Console interface is sufficient; optional original illustrations earn no separate marks.
Common brief and test templates.
tests: Invalid menu input allows recovery.
A resource boundary of zero has the agreed outcome.
Repeatable choices produce a hand-predicted final total.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.

options.title: Equipment loans database
options.pitch: Design a community equipment desk using invented borrowers and equipment.
requirements: Design Borrower, Category, Equipment and Loan entities, including repeat loans and optional return dates.
Explain the normalisation decisions, document keys/domains and create the relational database.
Implement joined loan reports, aggregate inventory reports and safe insert/update/delete operations. Test constraints and recovery.
resources: SQLite or school-approved RDBMS; DB Browser for SQLite is optional.
Included flat source CSV, relationship prompt and SQL TODO file.
Existing unit 2 workbook provides practice, not a private marking key.
tests: Borrower B01 and equipment E01 can have repeated loans with different loan IDs.
A loan referring to missing equipment is rejected when foreign keys are enabled.
Returned loans disappear from the active-loans report, while history remains.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: Community festival bookings
options.pitch: Manage fictional sessions, venues and participant bookings for a community festival.
requirements: Design Participant, Venue, Session and Booking entities, resolving participant-to-session multiplicity.
Document a normalised design, keys, domains and field-level validation before implementation.
Create joined booking reports and attendance totals. Demonstrate changes and test invalid references.
resources: SQLite; synthetic participants/session records; common design workbook.
Teacher supplies venue capacities and an unambiguous booking rule.
No online payments or real participant information.
tests: One participant can book different sessions but cannot duplicate the same booking.
Unknown participant/session references fail.
A session with no bookings behaves as the report specification states.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

requirements: Model CustomerAlias, DeviceType, Device and Appointment with a documented scope.
Use a four-entity design, keys, relationships and normalisation evidence.
Produce joined appointment lists, totals by repair category and tested data changes.
resources: SQLite; invented records only; common test and data-dictionary templates.
No personal device contents, passwords or actual customer details.
Teacher supplies a small flat input table for normalisation.
tests: A device can have multiple appointments.
Deleting a referenced device follows an explicitly chosen integrity rule.
Totals match a small hand-counted fixture.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: VR lab loans and bookings

Track invented asset labels and current loans without collecting headset-account information.

Optional teacher demonstration of a real asset workflow.
Use the equipment pack structure with renamed fields and a fresh issued dataset.
tests: A returned device becomes available under the agreed rule.
An unknown asset ID fails validation.
The overdue-date boundary matches the written specification.
routes: SQL workspace and documented workflows: a complete RDBMS solution is the baseline.
Optional Python console interface using SQL, if already taught.
Optional approved desktop or local browser interface with the same database evidence.

options.title: Pygame warehouse planner
options.pitch: Build a warehouse training simulation for a fictional client using a grid and movable objects.
requirements: Represent warehouse occupancy in a two-dimensional array. Define student-authored classes with attributes and methods, using inheritance where it serves the design.
Use a dictionary for item lookup and implement the selected search/sort behaviour in the core logic rather than only calling a library.
Separate model from rendering, validate commands and retain a repeatable command replay. Evaluate the client’s success criteria.
resources: Python 3; Pygame optional; keyboard input and a simple original grid display.
Included warehouse-logic.py contracts, layout.csv, items.csv and command fixtures.
A console grid is an equivalent route to the same evidence.
tests: Moving into a blocked grid cell leaves the object in its original cell.
Coordinates outside the grid fail safely.
Replay the same command sequence to reproduce the same final grid.

options.title: Python experiments: evacuation model
options.pitch: Create a fictional grid simulation comparing route rules for a safety-training client.
requirements: Use a two-dimensional environment and classes for agents or barriers. Document individual responsibilities and interactions.
Implement deterministic movement, conflict and exit rules and a dictionary of agent states.
Compare rule sets against repeatable fixtures. Distinguish simulation assumptions from claims about real emergency safety.
resources: Python standard library; Pygame optional for display.
Teacher-supplied tiny grid and movement rules to limit scope.
No real movement tracking or real evacuation validation.
tests: An agent never enters a blocked or out-of-bounds cell.
A defined simultaneous conflict has a deterministic result.
An empty agent list terminates with the stated summary.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.pitch: Build a scheduling assistant for fictional club activities.
requirements: Use a two-dimensional room/period table and classes for sessions and resources.
Use dictionary lookup and a student-written taught search or sort routine in a meaningful workflow.
Validate conflicts, expose unresolved scheduling cases and evaluate the chosen strategy with test fixtures.
resources: Python standard library; synthetic room/session CSVs prepared by the teacher.
A bounded rule-based scheduler is sufficient; no advanced optimisation library required.
Common class/interface and trace templates.
tests: Two sessions cannot occupy the same room and period.
A session too large for every room stays unassigned with a reason.
Tied priorities follow a documented deterministic rule.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

requirements: Use a two-dimensional arena and classes for robots, with at least one justified specialisation or interface decision.
Store commands or robot lookup in a dictionary and process movement through tested methods.
Implement a bounded experiment and produce a client evaluation based on traceable results.
resources: Python 3; Pygame optional; synthetic arena and command files.
No physical robot required and no marks for hardware expense.
Teacher supplies collision and turn-order rules before issue.
tests: A robot at a boundary cannot leave the arena.
Commands for an unknown robot are rejected.
An empty command file ends without an infinite loop.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.pitch: Implement a Python grid-based training simulator from invented VR event records. The assessable program runs on a normal PC.
requirements: Create a two-dimensional training environment and classes for participants or checkpoints.
Read synthetic event records, use dictionary lookup and validate coordinates and event sequences.
Evaluate outcomes through deterministic replay. Optional headset observation informs requirements but is not the assessed Python implementation.
resources: Python 3; supplied invented event CSV with tick, alias, row, column and action.
Optional Quest observation/casting with approved app and IT setup.
Native Quest deployment would be a separate extension with a different toolchain.
tests: Replay identical events to produce identical state.
An invalid coordinate is rejected and recorded.
Missing checkpoints produce the agreed incomplete-training outcome.
routes: Console or text interface: assess the same logic and evidence.
Desktop interface: optional Pygame for games/simulations, or a school-approved GUI for tools.
Local browser interface: optional only if already taught; keep the Python/SQL core assessable.

options.title: VR lab booking and maintenance system
options.pitch: Develop an integrated Python/SQL system for a fictional shared-headset laboratory.
requirements: Model five related entities: BorrowerAlias, DeviceModel, Device, Booking and Maintenance. Explain keys, relationships and normalisation.
Create a Python interface that executes parameterised SQL for bookings, updates and reports. Include meaningful multi-table joins, grouped totals and calculated output.
Test integrity, a transaction that rolls back on failure, backup restoration and role/privacy decisions. Use synthetic asset and borrower data.
resources: Python sqlite3 and SQLite; no headset needed to earn any mark.
Included devices.csv, borrowers.csv, bookings.csv, schema-todo.sql and app-todo.py.
Optional headset observation only after school approval.
tests: A booking for an unknown device fails referential integrity.
A duplicate/conflicting booking follows the specified rejection rule.
A failed multi-step update rolls back and leaves earlier data unchanged.
routes: Python console interface using SQL: the baseline integrated solution.
Optional Python desktop GUI using the same database core.
Optional Python-backed local browser interface if already taught; retain the same SQL evidence.
